### 2026-10-10 – October 8: I finished the Schematic and all the connections

**10.7h**

October 8: I finished the Schematic and all the connections

After I researched, I put the components in KiCad using a Python script that using the LCSC number it adds the Symbol and the footprint so I added all the components

This is the USB-C that will work as port for charge my phone and to charge the powerbank

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZV79nHQevzH7YyWPkr6cicoh4QURYKVN/d2eb275e4d6f93b52911d81084849876b4502dc5ff3bea851f73ce104a26678b.png)

Is connected to the IP5306 that will work as a component for the power management and it's the one of the best of its kind with powerbanks

The next component that I'll be using is the ATTINY85-20SU that its the microcontroller that will control The RGB showing the status of charge and control the button depending of the press; it will turn on/off show the current charge

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZV79nHQevzH7YyWPkr6cicoh4QURYKVN/0148c6af6d4026dc78c52ba2be3277f82943c94b657a507929c11004aceeae77.png)

The next one is the HOLTEK HT7333-3 that will be used as a voltage regulator for the overcharges and discharges

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZV79nHQevzH7YyWPkr6cicoh4QURYKVN/cd35c06a2bbfbe48891e599852c3b494595bf66febd8cec2b6f867ac8a20d50e.png)

After that I assigned the footprints which was a huge challenge just because some footprints were not the right ones for the components for that I had to search them on EasyEda to download them and then import them into KiCad using the footprint editor

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZV79nHQevzH7YyWPkr6cicoh4QURYKVN/9b29575c4b615a2a1c2aa8253231f9879dfb95a1e8a2357e60ff59cc5c98eba9.png)

This is one of the imported footprints

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZV79nHQevzH7YyWPkr6cicoh4QURYKVN/03b638f7a72fce2b7b947fd7b7f75841b8a354a5cecad7b7018f9f9ad7e0a047.png)

Its the footprint for the IP5306

Right after that I decided to stop and take some rest (which turned into a 9-hour nap) for all the day I spent 6.8 Hours

I began with the designing of the PCB which was one of the hardest parts of the project just because I didn't know how to put the components so that it would look good but KiCad crashed once while I was trying to save it

Here its the USB-C and the IP5306 in the PCB
